title: Defense witness: Cale88 has zero employees in 2024, two in 2025
summary: Cale88 Foods Corporation, a listed business interest of Vice President Sara Duterte"s husband, Manases Carpio, in their joint wealth statement, recorded zero employees in 2024 and two employees in…

blocks.text: Cale88 Foods Corporation, a listed business interest of Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband, Manases Carpio, in their joint wealth statement, recorded zero employees in 2024 and two employees in 2025, a defense witness said Friday.

Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo of DTI’s Industry Development and Investment Promotions Group made the testimony during the cross-examination of private prosecutor Erwin Matib wherein the witness was confronted with General Information Sheet (GIS) submitted by Cale88 to the Board of Investments (BOI).

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero allowed the prosecution to confront Rodolfo, who also serves as the BOI’s Managing Head, with Cale88 Foods Corp. GIS for years 2024 and 2025 because he was familiar with such documents. Cale88 Foods Corp. changed ownership to Pikimong Pikimong Philippines Corp.
Asked by Matib how many rank-and-file employees Cale88 Foods Corp. had in 2024 based on GIS, Rodolfo said, “Wala po.” (None.)
Matib then asked Rodolfo if Cale88 Foods Corp. had a manpower complement in 2024 based on GIS, to which Rodolfo replied, “Wala rin po.” (There’s also none.)
Likewise, Rodolfo said he did not see any Cale88 Foods Corp. submission on its employees’ Social Security System and PhilHealth benefits.
He also explained that the BOI would not readily know the list of employees of a business entity unless the company applies for an incentive before the BOI.
“Ang pangbangga kasi namin iyong incentives. Pag nag-avail po sila ng incentive, hihingin po namin ‘yun (list of employees),” Rodolfo said.
(We base it on the incentives. If a firm seeks an incentive, we’ll ask for a list of incentives.)
“Dahil hindi naman siya nag-avail na incentive, wala pong pang bangga ho,” Rodolfo added.
(Because they did not avail of an incentive, we won’t have that record [of employees].)

Rodolfo earlier said during the same impeachment proceedings that based on Cale88 Foods Corp.’s BOI form submissions, its number of employees was reduced from 201 in 2024 to 50 in 2025 because of the change in ownership.

Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro of Batangas, in a separate interview, noted that such a discrepancy in Cale88 Foods Corp. submissions proves that the testimony of the prosecution witness and CPA-lawyer Alex Cabrera is an implausible business model.

“We saw the inconsistency [in submitted documents]. When you say it is an implausible business model, it does not necessarily mean a zero operation. We have to read that terminology on the basis of the entire procedure of the expert witness. For me, the fact that BIR documents (GIS) do not tally with the data with BOI makes it an implausible business model already,” Luistro told reporters.

“Because we need to be very consistent on the business data that we are submitting to the government agencies such as the DTI, Securities and Exchange Commission, and take note of the inward remittances reported by the AMLC (Anti-Money Laundering Council). Implausible is a very general term, and it could mean as well that inconsistent data or information which are being submitted or at the very least shown by the different government agencies,” Luistro added.

Defense witness and AML Consulting PH head, Atty. Rainer Dela Fuente, earlier testified that there were red flags in Cale88 Foods Corporation operations given that the firm only has two employees, received P319 million remittances from China and recorded 757 covered transactions and suspicious transactions worth P1.2 billion based on AMLC records.
Dela Fuente, however, said such red flags are not automatically illegal. —LDF, GMA News
